overview.text: The Walt Disney Company is an American entertainment and media company whose beginnings trace to brothers Walt and Roy Disney’s 1923 cartoon studio. On October 16 that year, Walt signed a distribution contract for the Alice Comedies, which featured a real-life girl adventuring in a cartoon world; the venture eventually became the company known today. Disney’s early fame grew around Mickey Mouse, whose 1928 cartoon Steamboat Willie used synchronized sound and helped establish the character as a lasting company symbol. Today the business extends beyond animation and films: its operations include entertainment media and streaming, ESPN, and experiences such as theme parks, resorts, cruises, vacations, and consumer products, linking stories with places and merchandise.

key_facts.text: The company’s beginnings are dated to October 16, 1923, when Walt Disney signed a contract to distribute the Alice Comedies; Walt and Roy Disney formed the studio together.
The Alice Comedies featured a real-life girl having adventures in a cartoon world.
Steamboat Willie, released in 1928, brought Mickey Mouse to prominence with synchronized sound; the story of Mickey’s creation has multiple versions, so its exact origin is uncertain.
The company currently identifies three core business segments: Disney Entertainment, ESPN, and Disney Experiences.
Disney Experiences includes theme parks and resorts, cruises and vacation experiences, and consumer products such as toys, clothing, and books.
